nodes.name: M oxide/hydroxide nanorod preparation
nodes.procedure: M-containing oxides/hydroxides nanorods were first prepared (Fig. S6–S15, ESI†)
nodes.source_text: M-containing oxides/hydroxides nanorods were first prepared (Fig. S6–S15, ESI†)

nodes.name: Polydopamine coating, carbonization, and acid etching
nodes.procedure: M-containing oxides/hydroxides nanorods were coated with polydopamine (Fig. S16, ESI†). Thermal treatment at 800 °C in argon was conducted to convert polydopamine to nitrogen-doped carbon with M-containing species supported thereon (Fig. S17–S26, ESI†). After sufficient acid etching under varied conditions, uniformly dispersed single atom M₁ or MₓOᵧ nanoclusters were formed on nitrogen-doped carbon support (denoted as M₁/NC or MₓOᵧ/NC, Fig. S27–S36, ESI†)

nodes.name: Ru impregnation and reduction
nodes.procedure: Ru precursors were further impregnated onto the M₁/NC or the MₓOᵧ/NC. At last, the MₓOᵧ–Ruₙ/NC catalyst and the M₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst were acquired individually through hydrogen reduction at 300 °C (Fig. 2 and Fig. S37–S41, ESI†)

nodes.characterization_summary: AC HAADF-STEM images show MₓOᵧ nanoclusters with average particle size ~1 nm evenly distributed around ultrafine Ruₙ nanoclusters (~1 nm) for ZnO-Ruₙ/NC, Fe₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC, MoO₃-Ruₙ/NC, Sm₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC, and La₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed by the aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM (AC HAADF-STEM) images and energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDS) elementary mapping images of the MₓOᵧ–Ruₙ/NC catalysts in Fig. 2a–e, the MₓOᵧ nanoclusters with an average particle size of about 1 nm are evenly distributed around the ultrafine Ruₙ nanoclusters (~1 nm), agreeing with the MₓOᵧ–Ru₁₃ model.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images, EDS mapping, and 3D surface tomographic profiles show M₁ single atoms uniformly located around ultrafine Ruₙ nanoclusters for Zn₁-Ruₙ/NC, Fe₁-Ruₙ/NC, Mo₁-Ruₙ/NC, Sm₁-Ruₙ/NC, and La₁-Ruₙ/NC catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: these characterization techniques coupled with the 3D surface tomographic profiles also suggest that the M₁ single atoms in the M₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst are uniformly located around the ultrafine Ruₙ nanoclusters, as indicated in Fig. 2f–j, which is in line with the M₁–Ru₁₃ model mentioned above.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping confirms uniform distribution of M, Ru, N, C, O elements in all MₓOᵧ–Ruₙ/NC and M₁–Ruₙ/NC catalysts (Fig. 2a–j).
nodes.evidence_snippet: energy-dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDS) elementary mapping images of the MₓOᵧ–Ruₙ/NC catalysts in Fig. 2a–e... HAADF-STEM images, EDS elementary mapping images, and 3D surface tomographic profiles of the Zn₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst, Fe₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst, Mo₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst, Sm₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst and La₁–Ruₙ/NC catalyst

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES spectra (Ru K-edge, Zn K-edge, Fe K-edge, Mo K-edge, Sm L-edge, La L-edge) confirm oxidation states and coordination environments matching theoretical MₓOᵧ–Ru₁₃ and M₁–Ru₁₃ models (Fig. 3, Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The microstructure of the synthesized MₓOᵧ–Ruₙ/NC and M₁–Ruₙ/NC catalysts were further confirmed by corresponding X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy characterizations, as displayed in Fig. 3a–y and Fig. S43–S47 (ESI†), and Table S1 (ESI†)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS spectra show Zn LMM Auger (ZnO-Ruₙ/NC), Fe 2p (Fe₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC), Mo 3d (MoO₃-Ruₙ/NC), Sm 3d (Sm₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC), La 3d (La₂O₃-Ruₙ/NC) characteristic peaks confirming metal oxidation states.
nodes.evidence_snippet: (a) Zn LMM Auger spectrum of the ZnO-Ruₙ/NC catalyst. (f) Fe 2p XPS spectrum of the Fe₂O₃–Ruₙ/NC catalyst. (k) Mo 3d XPS spectrum of the MoO₃–Ruₙ/NC catalyst. (p) Sm 3d XPS spectrum of the Sm₂O₃–Ruₙ/NC catalyst. (u) La 3d XPS spectrum of the La₂O₃–Ruₙ/NC catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution wavelet transform EXAFS confirms M single atoms in M₁–Ruₙ/NC catalysts (M=Zn,Fe,Mo,Sm,La) are coordinated with N atoms rather than O atoms (Fig. S48, Table S1).
nodes.evidence_snippet: the high-resolution wavelet transform (WT) EXAFS characterization, which is commonly used to examine the coordination environment of single atoms, was also conducted to determine whether the acquired M single atoms in the M₁–Ruₙ catalysts are coordinated with N or O. It was identified that the M single atoms in the M₁–Ruₙ catalysts are well coordinated with N atoms instead of O atoms, as indicated by the (WT) EXAFS spectra in Fig. S48 (ESI†)

nodes.characterization_summary: Nitrogen-doped carbon support shows BET specific surface area of 622 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: by virtue of the N-metal coordination and the large BET specific surface area of the support (622 m² g⁻¹, Fig. S49, ESI†)
